criteria.criterion: 2. Telegram initData validation preserved unchanged (tampered/missing/stale stay 401)
criteria.evidence: git diff ff92055~1..ff92055 --stat for apps/web/app/hq/lib and apps/web/app/hq/api shows only the 3 routes under api/ (6 insertions, 6 deletions), all comment or message-string edits. verify-init-data.ts is not in the diff. Browser-driven /hq with a Telegram.WebApp stub: freshly signed initData renders the org (34 nodes) and sends the authorization 'tma ...' header on both GET /hq/api/org-tree and POST /hq/api/action. criteria.criterion: 3. A normal browser reaches the same Mini view through the existing Google-auth path, no Telegram secret involved
criteria.evidence: Prod curl of https://holocene.delo.sh/mini returns 307 to accounts.google.com/o/oauth2 (the existing Google auth). /api/modules/org/tree is gated: the smoke shows 401 for a script without a session, which its GATED set accepts (302, 307 or 401). /mini against the container, which has no auth, renders the identical 34-node view, with GET /api/modules/org/tree and POST /api/modules/hermes-fleet/... calls, no authorization header on any request, and no Telegram SDK dependency. Limitation: I cannot complete a real Google login headlessly, so 'authenticated browser sees the view' is proven by the container run plus the prod 307 gate, not by a live signed-in session.

findings.summary: Expired Google session in browser mode never reaches the 'signed-out' state. The signedOut() check is dead code against the real Traefik forward-auth, and the user sees a wrong, circular banner.
findings.evidence: Measured in headless Chromium from a same-origin page on https://holocene.delo.sh: fetch('/api/modules/org/tree',{redirect:'manual'}) returns type 'basic', status 401, content-type text/plain, body 'Authentication required', redirected false. curl shows the cause: google-auth answers 307 for navigations or requests without Sec-Fetch-Mode, but 401 whenever 'Sec-Fetch-Mode: cors' is present, which every browser fetch() sends. signedOut() only tests res.type==='opaqueredirect' or res.redirected to an off-origin URL, and neither can happen. fetchOnce then takes the 401 branch: initDataRef.current is '' in browser mode, so the state becomes 'no-telegram'. With the tree request mocked to 401 text/plain, /mini shows 'Open this from Telegram, or use the browser version... In a browser, open holocene.delo.sh/mini'. That is circular, tells the user to open the page they are already on, and replaces the whole org view. Only a mocked 307 produced the intended 'Your Google sign-in expired' banner. The commit message claim 'an expired Google session shows a sign-in banner' is therefore untrue for real traffic. postAction and getAction in browser mode have the same hole. The 401 body is not JSON and signedOut is false, so the sheet shows the generic 'HTTP 401' instead of a sign-in message.
findings.fix: In browser mode, treat res.status === 401 (and 403) as signed-out in fetchOnce, postAction and getAction. Keep the opaqueredirect check as a secondary guard. Make the signed-out banner link to /mini, which navigates and so gets the 307 to Google. Consider pausing the 5s poll, or keeping the last tree visible, while signed out.

findings.summary: In browser mode a 503 from Traefik, the Next rewrite or the API is rendered as 'not wired up: set TELEGRAM_HQ_BOT_TOKEN'.
findings.evidence: fetchOnce maps any res.status===503 to the 'not-configured' banner, which is Telegram-only wording. The browser path never needs that token. A holocene-api restart or a Traefik 503 would send the operator to the wrong remedy.
findings.fix: Gate the 503 to not-configured on !browser. In browser mode use the generic 'Fleet API returned 503' error state.

findings.summary: mini-smoke does not cover the state-changing browser-mode surface, and its Google-auth assertions are weak.
findings.evidence: The script checks only GET /mini and GET /api/modules/org/tree for the Google gate. It never checks POST /hq/api/action without auth, nor POST /api/modules/hermes-fleet/agents/<nonexistent>/services/gateway/start without a cookie, although that route is what browser mode actually calls. I ran both by hand against prod: 401 and 307, which is correct. GATED=[302,307,401] accepts any 401, so a Next-level 401 would pass as 'behind Google auth'. Tampered and stale checks assert only the status, not reason 'bad signature' or 'expired initData'. Tampering works (the replace hits query_id 'mini-smoke' first, so the hash is invalid either way). Sorting by key with localeCompare matches verify's pairs.sort() for the keys used. The script exits 1 on failure; a run against the unauthenticated container failed 2 of 9 checks, as it should.
findings.fix: Add an unauthenticated POST to /hq/api/action (expect 401) and an unauthenticated POST to a nonexistent agent's service route (expect 307 or 401 with 'Authentication required'). Assert reason strings on the tampered and stale responses. For the Google checks, assert a Location header containing accounts.google.com, or the 'Authentication required' body.

findings.summary: The dialect guard is still meaningful but does not scan the new /mini route.
findings.evidence: dialect-guard.test.ts scans apps/web/app/hq only. The new browser-mode logic lives in hq-client.tsx, which is scanned and still pinned by its allowlist (legacy-ok-dialect, non-registry-payload-import). The new { ok:false, status:401, data } literals fall under the already-allowlisted legacy-ok-dialect reason. apps/web/app/mini holds only a layout and a thin page that imports MiniApp. The guard passes (89/89) and nothing was weakened. Browser mode consumes the raw org tree from /api/modules/org/tree, the same legacy payload the /hq relay already forwarded.
findings.fix: Optional: add apps/web/app/mini to the scanned dirs so a future dialect added there is caught.
